newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to stay out of open market.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to stay out of open market.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Thursday after adding substantial amounts of reserves to the banking system earlier in the week, analysts said.

"They've already put a fairly large amount of reserves in the banking sytsem and Fed funds are quite comfortable this morning and so we look for them to stay on the sidelines," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc.
The Fed added temporary reserves on Tuesday via nine-day system repurchase agreements totaling $2.955 billion.
On Wednesday, the Fed added reserves via overnight system repurchase agreements.
Fed funds were trading at 5-3/16 percent at midmorning on Thursday, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.

"We expect the Fed will stay out of the market," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co. "We think the nine-day system repurchase agreements they did on Tuesday will satisfy the add need for today."
